observations: Photo 0: a used inline four-cylinder petrol car engine sitting on the ground in a parts yard, with another engine behind it.
Photo 0: four coil-on-plug ignition coils on a black plastic valve cover, oil filler cap, plastic intake manifold, wiring harness, alternator and a ribbed drive belt pulley.
Photo 0: green paint marks sprayed over the valve cover and manifold, the kind used to tag imported used engines.
Photo 0: no maker's logo, engine code, displacement or serial number can be read; a faint shop watermark ending 'VENTURE' sits across the middle.
Only the top of the engine is shown; block, oil pan, timing side, compression and mileage are not shown.

read_from: photo 0 general shape only, no readable marking

claims.evidence: The layout in photo 0 is consistent with a Korean-made four-cylinder engine, but no maker's logo or engine code is readable, so origin and make are not shown.

risks.risk: Engine code and displacement unknown, and these set the price and which cars it fits.
risks.proof: Close, sharp photo of the engine code stamped on the block and the label or casting on the valve cover.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; engine type unknown

risks.risk: Engine does not run, has low compression, knocks or burns oil.
risks.proof: Clip of the engine running on a test stand, or a compression test reading per cylinder.

risks.risk: Cracked block, damaged oil pan or seized internals hidden below or behind.
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides and the underside of the engine.

risks.risk: Missing ancillaries, sensors or ECU that a buyer expects in a complete engine.
risks.proof: Seller list of what is included plus a photo of the full assembly.
risks.if_unproven: as bare engine with only the visible parts

proof_requests: Close photo of the engine code and serial stamped on the block.
Photo of any maker's logo or label on the valve cover or timing cover.
Clip of the engine running or turning over.
Photos of all sides and underneath.
response.reason: Photo 0 shows a used four-cylinder petrol engine but no maker, engine code or displacement can be read, and that code is what sets the price, so no worst-case price is possible until a clear photo of the stamped engine code is sent.
